The whole subject in one screen

Everything, condensed

01Signals, and what discrete time changes
  • Digital frequency f=FFsf = \frac{F}{F_{s}}f=Fs​F​; only −½ ≤ f ≤ ½ is distinct, and ω and ω + 2πk are the same signal.
  • A discrete sinusoid is periodic only if f is a ratio of whole numbers; write f = k/N in lowest terms and N is the period.
  • For a sum of sinusoids the period is the LCM of the individual periods.
  • Energy signal ⇒ E finite and P = 0. Power signal ⇒ E infinite and P finite. Every periodic signal is a power signal.
  • The fastest discrete oscillation is at ω = π: one sign change per sample. There is nothing faster.
02Sampling, aliasing and quantization
  • Sample faster than twice the highest frequency: Fs>2Fmax⁡F_s > 2 F_{\max}Fs​>2Fmax​. The Nyquist rate is 2Fmax⁡2 F_{\max}2Fmax​; the folding frequency is Fs2\frac{F_s}{2}2Fs​​.
  • Every frequency in the family F0+kFsF_{0} + k F_sF0​+kFs​ gives identical samples — that is aliasing.
  • To find the apparent frequency: form f = F/Fs, slide it into −½ ≤ f ≤ ½ by whole numbers, multiply back by Fs.
  • Aliasing is not recoverable: two components can land on the same digital frequency and add.
  • Quantization step D=xmax⁡−xmin⁡L−1D = \frac{x_{\max} - x_{\min}}{L - 1}D=L−1xmax​−xmin​​, error at most D/2, and SQNR = 1.76 + 6.02b dB — about 6 dB per bit.
03Discrete-time signals: writing them, moving them
  • Four notations for one signal — functional, tabular, sequence, graphical. In sequence form the arrow marks n = 0 and must be carried everywhere.
  • d(n)=u(n)−u(n−1)d(n) = u(n) - u(n - 1)d(n)=u(n)−u(n−1), and x(n)=∑kx(k)d(n−k)x(n) = \sum_{k} x(k) d(n - k)x(n)=∑k​x(k)d(n−k) — any signal is a row of weighted impulses. That identity is where convolution comes from.
  • x(n−k)x(n - k)x(n−k) delays to the right for positive k; x(−n)x(- n)x(−n) mirrors about the origin.
  • Fold and shift do not commute: rewrite as x(−(n+k))x(- (n + k))x(−(n+k)) first, then fold, then shift by what is left in the bracket.
  • Even part x(n)+x(−n)2\frac{x(n) + x(- n)}{2}2x(n)+x(−n)​, odd part x(n)−x(−n)2\frac{x(n) - x(- n)}{2}2x(n)−x(−n)​, and the odd part is always zero at n = 0.
04LTI systems and convolution
  • For an LTI system, h(n) is everything: causal ⇔ h(n) = 0 for n < 0, stable ⇔ ∑∣h(n)∣\sum \lvert h(n) \rvert∑∣h(n)∣ is finite. FIR is always stable.
  • y(n)=∑kx(k)h(n−k)y(n) = \sum_{k} x(k) h(n - k)y(n)=∑k​x(k)h(n−k) — break the input into impulses, add the answers.
  • Result length = n1 + n2 − 1, starting at (start of x + start of h).
  • Free check every time: ∑y=(∑x)(∑h)\sum y = \left( \sum x \right) \left( \sum h \right)∑y=(∑x)(∑h).
  • Cascade multiplies the responses (h1 ∗ h2); parallel adds them (h1 + h2).
  • Step response is the running sum of h; so h(n)=s(n)−s(n−1)h(n) = s(n) - s(n - 1)h(n)=s(n)−s(n−1) recovers the system from its step response.
05Difference equations and the total response
  • No feedback → FIR and always stable; feedback → IIR and the roots decide stability.
  • Total = natural + forced = zero-input + zero-state — two different cuts of the same answer, and zero-state still contains a transient.
  • Homogeneous: solve λN+a1λN−1+⋯=0\lambda^{N} + a_{1} \lambda^{N - 1} + \dots = 0λN+a1​λN−1+⋯=0; particular: guess the shape of the input; then fit the constants from y(0), y(1) computed by the equation.
  • Impulse response: homogeneous solution with h0(0)=1h_{0}(0) = 1h0​(0)=1, then h(n)=b0h0(n)+b1h0(n−1)+…h(n) = b_{0} h_{0}(n) + b_{1} h_{0}(n - 1) + \dotsh(n)=b0​h0​(n)+b1​h0​(n−1)+….
  • The inverse system swaps x and y — and swaps poles with zeros, so an IIR system inverts to an FIR one.
  • Always verify a closed-form answer by running the recursion for three samples. It takes thirty seconds.
06The z-transform and the ROC
  • X(z)=∑x(n)z−nX(z) = \sum x(n) z^{-n}X(z)=∑x(n)z−n, and the answer is incomplete without its ROC.
  • anu(n)a^{n} u(n)anu(n) and −anu(−n−1)- a^{n} u(- n - 1)−anu(−n−1) have the identical X(z) and differ only in the ROC — note the minus sign on the left-sided one.
  • ROC is a ring centred on the origin and never contains a pole: right-sided → outside the outermost pole, left-sided → inside the innermost.
  • Two-sided signals give an annulus, which may be empty — and then no z-transform exists.
  • The workhorse property is the delay: x(n-k) <-> z^-k X(z), which turns a difference equation into algebra in one line.
  • Convolution becomes multiplication: x ∗ h <-> X(z)H(z).
07The inverse z-transform
  • Before inverting anything, find the ROC. It decides the sign and the side of every term.
  • Partial fractions: expand X(z)/z, split, then multiply back by z — that leaves terms in the A1−pz−1\frac{A}{1 - p z^{-1}}1−pz−1A​ shape.
  • Term by term: ROC outside the pole → +Apnu(n)+ A p^{n} u(n)+Apnu(n); ROC inside the pole → −Apnu(−n−1)- A p^{n} u(- n - 1)−Apnu(−n−1), with the minus sign.
  • M poles at distinct radii give M + 1 possible ROCs and M + 1 different signals from one X(z).
  • Long division in descending powers of z gives a causal sequence; ascending powers gives an anti-causal one.
  • A complex pole pair re±jω0r e^{\pm j\omega_0}re±jω0​ gives rncos⁡(ω0n+ϕ)r^{n} \cos(\omega_0 n + \phi)rncos(ω0​n+ϕ) — radius sets the decay, angle sets the oscillation.
08System function, poles, zeros and stability
  • H(z) = numerator over denominator; zeros from the top, poles from the bottom, and only poles decide stability.
  • Causal ⇔ ROC is outside the outermost pole. Stable ⇔ ROC contains |z| = 1. Two separate tests.
  • Causal and stable together ⇔ every pole strictly inside the unit circle. Nothing else.
  • M distinct pole radii give M + 1 possible ROCs — a complex conjugate pair is one radius, not two.
  • A pole’s radius sets how fast its mode decays; its angle sets the frequency it resonates at.
  • A zero on the unit circle at angle ω0 puts an exact null in the frequency response at ω0.
09Frequency response
  • Frequency response = H(z) evaluated at z=ejωz = e^{j\omega}z=ejω, legal only if the ROC contains the unit circle.
  • The DTFT is continuous in ω and periodic with period 2π — only −π to π is distinct.
  • Use ∣1−ae−jω∣2=1−2acos⁡ω+a2\lvert 1 - a e^{-j\omega} \rvert^{2} = 1 - 2 a \cos \omega + a^{2}∣1−ae−jω∣2=1−2acosω+a2; take magnitudes and angles of numerator and denominator separately.
  • Filter type in two substitutions: H(+1)H(+ 1)H(+1) is the DC gain, H(−1)H(- 1)H(−1) is the gain at ω = π. Bigger at +1 means low-pass.
  • A zero on the unit circle gives an exact null; a pole on it gives infinite gain and no BIBO stability.
  • Steady state: a sinusoid in gives the same frequency out, scaled by |H| and shifted by ∠H.
10The DFT and its properties
  • X(k)=∑x(n)WNnkX(k) = \sum x(n) W_{N}^{nk}X(k)=∑x(n)WNnk​ with WN=e−j2πNW_{N} = e^{- \frac{j 2 \pi}{N}}WN​=e−Nj2π​; for N = 4 that is just powers of −j.
  • Two free checks on every DFT: X(0)=∑x(n)X(0) = \sum x(n)X(0)=∑x(n), and for real x(n) X(N−k)=conj (X(k))X(N - k) = \text{conj}\, (X(k))X(N−k)=conj(X(k)) with X(N2)X\left( \frac{N}{2} \right)X(2N​) purely real.
  • The DFT is periodic in k with period N — asking for X(4)..X(7) of a 4-point DFT is asking for X(0)..X(3) again.
  • Multiplying two DFTs gives circular convolution; the tail wraps round and adds to the front.
  • Zero-pad both signals to L≥N+M−1L \ge N + M - 1L≥N+M−1 and circular convolution equals the linear answer.
  • Zero padding adds dots, not resolution. Resolution needs a longer record; bin spacing is FsN\frac{F_s}{N}NFs​​.
11The FFT
  • The FFT computes the same DFT; the saving comes from WNk+N2=−WNkW_{N}^{k + \frac{N}{2}} = - W_{N}^{k}WNk+2N​​=−WNk​ and WNk+N=WNkW_{N}^{k + N} = W_{N}^{k}WNk+N​=WNk​.
  • Radix-2 costs (N2)log⁡2N\left( \frac{N}{2} \right) \log_{2} N(2N​)log2​N multiplications and N log2 N additions, in log2 N stages of N/2 butterflies — against N2N^{2}N2 and N(N−1)N(N - 1)N(N−1) direct.
  • At N = 8 that is 12 multiplications instead of 64 (5.3×); at N = 1024 it is 5,120 instead of 1,048,576 (205×).
  • DIT splits the input, twiddle before the add, bit-reversed input. DIF splits the output, twiddle after the add, bit-reversed output. Identical cost.
  • Both work in place in about 5N/2 words — bit reversal is the price paid for that.
  • The IFFT is the same flow graph with conjugated twiddles and a final divide by N; the operation count is unchanged.
12FIR filter design
  • FIR: no feedback, always stable, linear phase exactly when h(n)=±h(M−1−n)h(n) = \pm h(M - 1 - n)h(n)=±h(M−1−n), delay M−12\frac{M - 1}{2}2M−1​. Four types; Type 2 has H(π)=0H(\pi) = 0H(π)=0, Types 3 and 4 have H(0) = 0.
  • Window method: hd(n)=sin⁡(ωc(n−τ))π(n−τ)h_{d}(n) = \frac{\sin(\omega_c(n - \tau))}{\pi(n - \tau)}hd​(n)=π(n−τ)sin(ωc​(n−τ))​, hd(τ)=ωcπh_{d}(\tau) = \frac{\omega_c}{\pi}hd​(τ)=πωc​​, times ω(n)\omega(n)ω(n). HP = d(n−τ)d(n - \tau)d(n−τ) − LP for odd M.
  • Windows: rect −21 dB, Hann −44, Hamming −53, Blackman −74 stopband; main lobe k2πM\frac{k 2 \pi}{M}Mk2π​ with k = 2, 4, 4, 6. Gibbs = 9% whatever M.
  • Length: M=k2πws−wpM = \frac{k 2 \pi}{ws - wp}M=ws−wpk2π​. Kaiser: A=−20log⁡10(δ)A = - 20 \log_{10}(\delta)A=−20log10​(δ), beta from A, M≥A−7.9514.36dfM \ge \frac{A - 7.95}{14.36 df}M≥14.36dfA−7.95​.
  • Frequency sampling: h(n)=(1M)[H(0)+2∑∣H(k)∣cos⁡(2πk(n−τ)M)]h(n) = \left( \frac{1}{M} \right) \left[ H(0) + 2 \sum \lvert H(k) \rvert \cos\left( \frac{2 \pi k(n - \tau)}{M} \right) \right]h(n)=(M1​)[H(0)+2∑∣H(k)∣cos(M2πk(n−τ)​)], exact at the samples; a 0.4 transition sample buys about 20 dB.
  • Differentiator hd=cos⁡(π(n−τ))n−τh_{d} = \frac{\cos(\pi(n - \tau))}{n - \tau}hd​=n−τcos(π(n−τ))​, Hilbert hd=[1−cos⁡(π(n−τ))]π(n−τ)h_{d} = \frac{[1 - \cos(\pi(n - \tau))]}{\pi(n - \tau)}hd​=π(n−τ)[1−cos(π(n−τ))]​: both antisymmetric, both H(0) = 0.
13The paper itself
  • Five questions, 30 marks, ninety minutes, and the same skeleton for three years running.
  • Four areas carry about 24 of the 30 marks: DFT or FFT, a difference equation, a z-transform with its ROC, and a frequency response.
  • The FFT question is the one that moves — learn the counting formulas, both decimations, the inverse, and one non-radix-2 case.
  • Most-punished errors: no ROC, the missing minus on the anti-causal term, bit-reversing the wrong end, and treating a repeated DFT value as a longer DFT.
  • Spend the last ten minutes on free checks: the convolution sum check, X(0)=∑x(n)X(0) = \sum x(n)X(0)=∑x(n), and three samples of the recursion.
  • Where a question is ambiguous, state your assumption in one line and answer it. A stated assumption scores; a blank does not.

That is the entire revision set — 75 lines. If a line does not make sense, the chapter it came from is one tap away, and the full course is behind that.
